title: the compiled floor agrees with the engine on fresh tasks at lower cost
intention: cairn.machines.learning_block.validate runs a compiled floor and the engine path side by side over fresh payloads (inputs absent from the compiled corpus) and reports, per payload, both outcomes and each path's cost (inference calls, wall time); a floor that disagrees or abstains on a fresh payload fails, so a memorizing compile cannot pass.
why: Child 3 of d6cacb63868b (proof-validate-compiled-vs-model). The parent's falsifier: 'the compiled floor agrees with the model path on FRESH tasks at measurably lower cost. A compile that memorizes FAILS validate on fresh tasks (Law 8).' Measured 2026-11-13, the one corpus that meets child 2's trigger is one question repeated plus 3 escalations, which is exactly the corpus a memorizing compile would pass on if validate replayed it.
traces_to: Law 8 (nothing enters proven-space without a proof a hollow build couldn't pass: a lookup table is the hollow build here) and Law 3 ('cheaper and still right' is measured, never hoped).
how: D1: validate.py's validate_floor(floor, spec, fresh_payloads, *, model_path=run_block) runs each fresh payload through both paths and returns a report: per payload the two outcomes, agree/disagree/abstain, and each path's inference calls and wall ms. D2: the proof builds a fixture block whose model path is stubbed to count one inference call per backfill, compiles a floor through child 2's compile_floor, and runs a memorizing floor (a lookup of the traced inputs) beside it. Built after child 2 is PROVED.

clauses.claim: validate_floor over fresh payloads (none in the compiled corpus) reports, for each, the floor's outcome beside the engine path's, and on the fixture block the compiled floor agrees on every fresh payload
a memorizing floor, a lookup of the corpus's traced inputs only, fails validate_floor on the same fresh payloads, the report naming each disagreement or abstention
the report measures each path's cost: the floor makes 0 inference calls and fewer wall ms than the stubbed model path, which counts one inference call per backfill

decisions.text: D1: new validate.py: validate_floor(floor, spec, fresh_payloads, *, model_path=run_block) -> report; refuses a fresh payload that appears in the floor's source runs (fresh means fresh); cost is counted per path (inference calls through the injected model path's counter, wall ms by time.perf_counter).

D2: proof test_the_compiled_floor_agrees_on_fresh_tasks.py, one tooth per clause, every trace and floor under a scratch root; the memorizing floor is built in the proof as the hollow build validate must fail.

out: child 2's compile (its own ticket; this child reads its floor through compile_floor)

measured.saw: librarian-ask holds 7 engine_run training traces; 4 of them are one question ('Is CC allowed to seal concept-pieces on its own?') with one winner, 0:5a34fcee46b7, every time; the other 3 are backfill runs (backfills=3, reason 'learned'), all 3 escalated to the operator, carries_his_answer killing 5, 6 and 5 of their 6 candidates; every candidates_log entry carries only name, outcome, killed_by and outranked_by, no provides
measured.how: read ~/.cairn/devices/learning_block/0/traces/librarian-ask.jsonl line by line (Linux, akiendell), and survey_the_corpus() from cairn/machines/learning_block/probes/engine_trace_corpus.py: librarian-ask 7 runs, 7 answer all five; intentions_model_compiler 2 runs

measured.saw: engine.py builds candidates_log from name, outcome, killed_by, outranked_by (cairn/machines/learning_block/engine.py run_block); the candidate's provides, the only features _satisfies reads, is dropped from the record
